newsitem.title: USA: RESEARCH ALERT - Merrill ups IBM.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Merrill ups IBM.

text.p: -- Merrill Lynch analyst Dan Mandresh upgraded International Business Machines Corp to near-term buy from neutral and kept the long-term rating at buy, according to a Merrill source.
-- increased the earnings estimate to $12.50 per share from $11.95, and kept the 1998 estimate at $14, the source said.
-- also, Salomon Brothers analyst John Jones reiterated a strong buy rating on the stock.
-- said he believes that Wall Street's consensus estimates of $12.18 for 1997 and $14.09 for 1998 "will trend upwards over time to be more in line with our expectations."
-- Jones maintained estimates of $12.50 for 1997 and $14.50 for 1998.

Jones said, "We view IBM statements that they are cautiously optimistic as being positive. They have better revenue and profit visibility due to the mix of business shifting to services and recurring revenue streams.
-- "IBM has positioned itself to deliver high single-digit constant currency revenue growth which should drive mid-double-digit earnings growth."
-- Shares in the company closed Wednesday at 142-3/8 and IBM announced strong first quarter results following the market's close. In early pre-open trade, shares climbed to 148.
